subject.title: [BUG]: Browser tool: `snapshot` returns page content before scroll, ignoring viewport position

question: Should browser `snapshot` become visible-viewport scoped after scroll, or should OpenClaw add an explicit visible-viewport read mode while keeping full-tree snapshots as the default?
rationale: The current code can be changed mechanically, but the choice affects model-facing browser semantics, compatibility with full-page automation workflows, and how agents reason about page state after scrolling.

options.title: Add Explicit Visible-Viewport Mode
options.body: Introduce a viewport-scoped read with scroll/viewport metadata and keep full/raw tree snapshots available for compatibility.

options.title: Change Snapshot Default
options.body: Make ordinary `snapshot` return the visible viewport after scroll and require callers to opt into full/raw tree reads.

options.title: Keep Current Full-Tree Contract
options.body: Document that snapshots are full UI trees and direct users to labels/screenshots or a future separate issue for viewport reads.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Visible-Viewport Mode
recommendation.body: Introduce a viewport-scoped read with scroll/viewport metadata and keep full/raw tree snapshots available for compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser snapshot route, docs, and product-surface history make this the clearest owner for deciding the model-facing contract.
